sections.sentence: 6 contracts, each running exactly the build docs/REPRODUCIBLE-BUILD.md records; each still has a full-access key, so its holder can change it; all import the host functions that deploy code or change keys (near-sdk links them), so the code alone does not show it never will.

sources: host function names: nearcore runtime/near-vm-runner/src/imports.rs (crate near-vm-runner 0.38.1) and near-sdk-rs near-sys/src/lib.rs (crate near-sys 0.4.1), both in the owner's Cargo.lock; read 2026-11-13

only the account itself may deploy code, add or delete keys, delete itself or use a global contract: nearcore runtime/runtime/src/actions.rs check_actor_permissions (master, read 2026-11-13); near-primitives 0.38.1 src/errors.rs ActorNoPermission
a function-call key signs exactly one FunctionCall with no deposit: nearcore runtime/runtime/src/verifier.rs verify_function_call_permission (master, read 2026-11-13)

near-sdk 5.30.1 links every action host function into any contract that uses its Promise type (as cross-contract calls do): src/promise.rs PromiseAction::add handles every kind of action in one function
global contracts in view_account: near-primitives 0.38.1 src/views.rs AccountView (global_contract_hash, global_contract_account_id)

sections.title: NEAR AI's hardware evidence for the pinned model
sections.sentence: NEAR AI's z-ai/glm-5.3-flash ed25519 key is bound to a fresh Intel TDX quote carrying our nonce, and the GPU evidence with the same nonce passed NVIDIA's attestation; 6 parts stay UNVERIFIED (listed).

lines: NEAR AI attestation check, 2026-11-13T16:46:51.473Z. Read-only: no completion, no key.
model z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, signing scheme ed25519; our nonce 2699268afa699c363032e6b9406c49d569d60a9601999c05da484377de8f1fea (32 random bytes, new for this run)
GET https://cloud-api.near.ai/v1/attestation/report (provider=near): HTTP 200, 322790 bytes
Candidate 1 of 1
OK    nonce echoed: request_nonce is ours
OK    model and scheme: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, ed25519
OK    signer is 01's pin: 5a0210f2442c79355784f9de021985429561da5bacc3a4424b01ac52b7e0caff (01 §6.3)
Intel TDX quote (5006 bytes, version 4)
OK    PCK certificate chain: Intel SGX PCK Certificate -> Intel SGX PCK Platform CA -> Intel SGX Root CA; each signed by the next, the last is Intel's pinned root, all valid now
OK    quoting enclave report: signed by the PCK certificate's key
OK    attestation key: the quoting enclave's report data is sha256(attestation key || QE auth data)
OK    quote signature: the header and TD report are signed by the attestation key
OK    report data: the quote's report data is the signer's key then our nonce: it binds both
OK    debug mode: TD attributes 0000001000000000: debug off
OK    configuration: MRCONFIGID is 01, sha256(app_compose) c900dc7304663b73…, then zeros
OK    event log: RTMR3 replayed from 10 events equals the quote's

INFO  measured (not compared with any allowlist): MRTD df4d77c857de652b…, RTMR0 bc122d143ab76856…, RTMR1 4ae609807c765916…, RTMR2 bd67ab7554dc27ab…, os_image_hash 91fd5d69ccee3e5e…, compose_hash c900dc7304663b73…
NVIDIA GPU evidence (8 GPU(s), HOPPER)
OK    payload nonce: ours
POST NVIDIA NRAS /v3/attest/gpu: HTTP 200
OK    NRAS token signature: ES384, verifies with NVIDIA's published key
OK    GPU verdict: x-nvidia-overall-att-result is true
OK    GPU nonce: the token's eat_nonce is ours
OK    token time: valid now (nbf to exp)
OK    each GPU: 8 GPU token(s), each signed by NVIDIA, named by the overall token, nonce matched
UNVERIFIED, and why:

- Intel TCB status and security advisories: the quote's signature chain reaches Intel's root, so it was made on genuine Intel TDX hardware, but whether that platform is up to date needs Intel's collateral (TCB info, QE identity, revocation lists), which a DCAP verifier such as dcap-qvl (the one NEAR AI's docs name; 27 npm packages) fetches. Not added: no heavy new dependency.
- The quoting enclave's identity (its MRSIGNER and version against Intel's QE identity) and certificate revocation (Intel's PCK and root CRLs): the same collateral.

- The software measured: MRTD, RTMR0 to RTMR2, the OS image and the compose file are printed but not compared with an allowlist, and the image digests in the compose file are not checked for build provenance (NEAR AI's image-provenance flow needs a signed provenance statement per digest; not added). NEAR AI's docs leave the accepted measurements and builders to the reader's policy.
- That a given completion came from this instance: NEAR AI's docs warn that instances of one model share one signing key, so a matching signer does not show which instance answered.

- The GPU verdict is NVIDIA's (its reference-measurement and certificate-status checks are not redone here); its tokens are checked against NVIDIA's keys as published at the JWKS URL. The GPU evidence and the TDX quote are linked only by carrying the same nonce; NEAR AI's docs give no other binding.
- The gateway's own attestation (gateway_attestation): not checked. The signature the contract checks is the model's (provider_tee), made inside the model's TEE, so the gateway is not trusted for it.

RESULT  every check above passed: NEAR AI's z-ai/glm-5.3-flash ed25519 key is bound to a fresh Intel TDX quote with our nonce, and the GPU evidence with the same nonce passed NVIDIA's attestation. The parts listed as UNVERIFIED were not checked.
